rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The direct question to the Prophet affirms that God can abrogate a ruling and replace it with an equal or better one.
rows.anchor: الخطاب للنبي عليه السلام ومعنى الاستفهام تقرير أي : أنك تعلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the address includes everyone, the Prophet is singled out because no human knows more of these realities; prophetic knowledge dwarfs that of saints and all creation.
rows.anchor: وخصه عليه السلام بالخطاب مع أن غيره داخل في الخطاب أيضا حقيقة بناء على أن المقصود من الخطاب تقرير علم المخاطب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's ownership of the heavens and earth grounds His unrestricted power; they are singled out as the greatest and most wondrous created things.
rows.anchor: والملك تمام القدرة واستحكامها وتخصيص السموات والأرض بالذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording takes من as an emphatic particle and treats دون الله as a circumstantial phrase; ولي can mean close friend, patron, or one managing affairs, while نصير means helper and defender.
rows.anchor: وهو في حيز النصب على الحالية من الولي لأنه في الأصل صفة له فلما قدم انتصب حالا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A wali may be too weak to help, whereas a nasir may be an outsider to the person he assists.
rows.anchor: والفرق بين الولي والنصير أن الولي قد يضعف عن النصرة والنصير قد يكون أجنبيا عن المنصور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These assurances settle believers' hearts: they should rely on and turn only to God.
rows.anchor: والمقصود التسكين لقلوب المؤمنين بأن الله وليهم وناصرهم دون غيره فلا يجوز الاعتماد إلا عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Knowing God's power, sovereignty, and guardianship should yield certainty that He chooses what is best for believers, with trust, reliance, and surrender despite disbelievers' doubts about abrogation.
rows.anchor: هو الجزم والإيقان بأنه تعالى لا يفعل بهم في أمر من أمور دينهم أو دنياهم إلا ما هو خير لهم والعمل بموجبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heavens and earth are created with marvels that human minds cannot fully comprehend; the heavens are plural because they differ in kind or have separate orbits, while earths share the substance of soil.
rows.anchor: في إبداعهما على ما هما عليه مع ما فيهما من تعاجيب العبر وبدائع الصنايع التي يعجز عن فهمها عقول البشر

rows.speaker: ابن التمجيد
rows.claim: In the philosophers' account, each heaven's convex surface touches the concave surface above it, except the ninth sphere; authorities disagree whether the space above it is void.
rows.anchor: وعند الحكماء محدب كل سماء مماس لمقعر ما فوقه غير الفلك التاسع المسمى بالعرش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Night and day alternate, each following the other, and vary in length, darkness, and light.
rows.anchor: في تعاقبهما في الذهاب والمجيء يخلف أحدهما صاحبه إذا جاء أحدهما جاء الآخر خلفه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ships stay afloat despite their weight and the water's lightness, and move back and forth with a single wind; الفلك is a collective singular with feminine agreement.
rows.anchor: لا ترسب تحت الماء وهي ثقيلة كثيفة والماء خفيف لطيف وتقبل وتدبر بريح واحدة والفلك في الآية جمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ships carry useful goods: merchants profit from transport, and recipients benefit from what arrives.
rows.anchor: فإنهم ينتفعون بركوبها والحمل فيها للتجارة فهي تنفع الحامل لأنه يربح والمحمول إليه لأنه ينتفع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rain's origin is the direction above; 'heaven' can mean the celestial sphere or anything elevated, including clouds, and the phrase introduces water as a type.
rows.anchor: من لابتداء الغاية أي : من جهة السماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rain revives the land with plants, flowers, and trees; its death is the loss of crops and leaves as dryness takes hold.
rows.anchor: بأنواع النبات والأزهار وما عليها من الأشجار

rows.speaker: ابن الشيخ
rows.claim: The land's new beauty and growth are likened to an animal's life because both bring freshness, splendor, and increase.
rows.anchor: لما حصل للأرض بسبب ما نبت فيها من أنواع النبات حسن وكمال شبه ذلك بحياة الحيوان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Creatures are spread across the land after rain revives it, since fertility and rain sustain their growth and life.
rows.anchor: من كل حيوان يدب على وجهها من العقلاء وغيرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wind rotation includes changes in direction, warmth, force, and effects; another reported interpretation distinguishes winds of mercy from winds of punishment.
rows.anchor: في تقليبها في مهابها قبولا ودبورا وشمالا وجنوبا وفي كيفيتها حارة وباردة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas calls wind and water God's greatest armies and links the name الريح to its refreshing effect on people.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : أعظم جنود الله الريح والماء

rows.speaker: وكيع الجراح
rows.claim: Wakiʿ says that without wind and flies the world would become foul-smelling.
rows.anchor: قال وكيع الجراح : لولا الريح والذباب لأنتنت الدنيا

rows.speaker: شريح القاضي
rows.claim: Shurayh says each wind either heals someone ill or makes someone healthy ill.
rows.anchor: قال شريح القاضي : ما هبت الريح إلا لشفاء سقيم أو لسقم صحيح

rows.speaker: بكر بن عباس
rows.claim: Bakr says the four winds prepare every cloud drop: the east wind stirs it, the south gathers it, the west fertilizes it, and the north disperses it.
rows.anchor: قال بكر بن عباس : لا تخرج من السحاب قطرة حتى تعمل في السحاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The four primary winds come from the cardinal directions; winds between their bearings are called nakbāʾ because they veer from the primary courses.
rows.anchor: وأصول الرياح هذه الأربع فالشمال من ناحية الشام والجنوب تقابلها والصبا هي القبول من المشرق

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAmr counts eight winds: four bring mercy, while the barren and violent winds bring punishment on land or sea.
rows.anchor: وقال عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص : الرياح ثمان : أربع رحمة وأربع عذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Clouds are a divinely governed kind that moves quickly through the air; the noun is singular though treated collectively, and can be understood by singular or plural agreement.
rows.anchor: الغيم المذلل المنقاد الجاري على ما أجراه الله تعالى عليه وهو اسم جنس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cloud's suspension itself is wondrous: if light it should rise, and if dense it should fall.
rows.anchor: لأنه لو كان خفيفا لطيفا ينبغي أن يصعد ولو كثيفا يقتضي أن ينزل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The indefinite plural 'signs' magnifies their number and greatness; the delayed predicate permits the emphatic lām, and rational observers read these signs with minds and hearts.
rows.anchor: والتنكير للتفخيم كما وكيفا أي : آيات عظيمة كثيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People who reflect on these phenomena infer God's immense power and wisdom, recognize Him as creator, and affirm His oneness.
rows.anchor: أي : يتفكرون فيها وينظرون إليها بعيون العقول والقلوب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse rebukes polytheists who demanded a confirming sign: these changes already suffice, so their failure to recognize them shows poor judgment.
rows.anchor: وفيه تعريض لجهل المشركين الذين اقترحوا على الرسول آية تصدقه

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet warns that woe awaits whoever recites this verse without taking it to heart; the author explains the image as failing to consider it.
rows.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم "ويل لمن قرأ هذه الآية فمج بها"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The source ranks the declaration of divine oneness as the first level of tawhid from God's side, while humans begin with oneness of acts and are guided through attributes toward oneness of essence.
rows.anchor: أقدم توحيد من جهة الحق لا من جهتنا فإن أول رتبة التوحيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The source attributes the staged descent from tawhid of essence through attributes to acts, with creation as evidence, to al-Taʾwīlāt al-Qāshāniyya.
rows.anchor: ولما بعد هذا التوحيد عن مبالغ أفهام الناس نزل إلى مقام توحيد الصفات

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report says God may delay the request of a servant He loves to hear the servant's voice, but hasten the request of one He dislikes because He dislikes hearing him.
rows.anchor: "إن العبد يدعو الله سبحانه وهو يحبه فيقول : يا جبريل أخر حاجة عبدي

rows.speaker: سهل بن عبد الله
rows.claim: During a Baghdad drought, Muslims' unanswered supplication and Jews' answered supplication puzzled the caliph; Sahl explained that delay showed God's love for Muslims, while haste turned the disliked Jews away.
rows.anchor: فجاء سهل بن عبد الله وقال : يا أمير المؤمنين إنا معاشر المسلمين أحبنا الله

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A prophetic report names four supports of worldly life: scholars' knowledge, rulers' justice, the rich person's generosity, and the poor person's prayer.
rows.anchor: قال عليه السلام : "قوام الدنيا بأربعة أشياء : بعلم العلماء ، وعدل الأمراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Supplicants should invoke God's beautiful names and transmitted early prayers, and seek intercession through prophets, saints, and the righteous.
rows.anchor: وينبغي أن يسأل الله تعالى بأسمائه الحسنى العظام والأدعية المأثورة عن السلف الكرام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Places where prayers are expected to be answered include the Kaaba and sacred sites, during pilgrimage rites, at Zamzam, and at prophets' graves.
rows.anchor: وللدعاء أماكن يظن فيها الإجابة مثلا عند رؤية الكعبة والمساجد الثلاثة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some deny that any prophet's grave is certainly located, apart from the Prophet's; Abraham's is said to be within the enclosure but not precisely identified, while prayers near righteous graves are reported as tested under known conditions.
rows.anchor: وقيل : لا يصح قبر نبي بعينه سوى قبر نبينا عليه الصلاة والسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Placing the phrase 'on the night of the fast' first delays the expected ruling and makes the listener anticipate it, strengthening its effect when it arrives.
rows.anchor: تقديم الظرف على القائم مقام الفاعل للتشويق فإن ما حقه التقديم إذا أخر تبقى النفس مترقبة إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rafath originally means obscene speech, then speech about intimacy, and by euphemism sexual intercourse; Ibn Abbas says it covers whatever a man desires from a woman, including touch and kissing.
rows.anchor: أصل الرفث قول الفحش والتكلم بالقبح ثم جعل ذلك اسما لما يتكلم به عند النساء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preposition إلى is used with rafath because the expression implies afḍā, 'to become intimate with,' as in the cited description of spouses becoming intimate.
rows.anchor: عدي الرفث بإلى وإن كان المشهور تعديته بالباء تقول : رفثت بالمرأة لتضمنه معنى الإفضاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At first, a Ramadan fast allowed food, drink, and sex only until the late prayer or sleep; then all three became forbidden until the next night.
rows.anchor: وكان الرجل في ابتداء الإسلام إذا أمسى في رمضان حل له الأكل والشرب والجماع إلى أن يصلي العشاء الأخيرة أو يرقد

rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
rows.claim: After late prayer, Umar had intercourse with his wife, regretted it, and confessed to the Prophet; other men admitted the same lapse, and the verse brought relief to the community.
rows.anchor: ثم إن عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله تعالى عنه واقع أهله بعد صلاة العشاء الأخيرة فلما اغتسل أخذ يبكي

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet told Umar that he had not been worthy of that lapse, before the new permission came.
rows.anchor: فقال عليه السلام : "ما كنت جديرا بذلك يا عمر"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling spouses garments explains permission: they are closely intertwined, and each covers the other and protects them from sexual wrongdoing.
rows.anchor: وجعل كل من الرجل والمرأة لباسا للآخر لتجردهما عند النوم واعتناقهما واشتمال كل منهما على الآخر

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A hadith says marriage secures two thirds of a person's religion.
rows.anchor: كما جاء في الحديث "من تزوج فقد أحرز ثلثي دينه"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative reading understands spouses as each other's comfort or dwelling, like the verse saying that God made a mate so a person could find tranquility with her.
rows.anchor: أو المعنى هن سكن لكم وأنتم سكن لهن كما قال تعالى : {وجعل منها زوجها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's knowledge that people had been betraying themselves refers to His eternal knowledge.
rows.anchor: {علم الله} في الأزل {أنكم كنتم تختانون أنفسكم}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sex during prohibited fasting hours wrongs the self by risking punishment and losing reward; secretly disobeying a divine trust is treachery, as the cited warning says.
rows.anchor: تخونونها وتظلمونها بتعريضها للعقاب وتنقيص حظها من الثواب بمباشرة النساء

rows.speaker: صائب
rows.claim: A Persian couplet urges a trustee to guard God's entrusted jewel from thieves and not sleep.
rows.anchor: ترابكوهر دل كرده اند امانت دار زدزد امانت حق را نكاه دار مخسب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God accepted their repentance and erased the trace of their earlier breach.
rows.anchor: قبل توبتكم وتجاوز عنكم لما تبتم مما اقترفتموه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Now marks the time after the prohibition was repealed; intercourse means joining skin to skin and stands for sex and its preliminaries.
rows.anchor: لما نسخ التحريم ظرف لقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the earlier ban on eating, drinking, and intercourse came from prophetic Sunnah, the verse proves scripture can abrogate Sunnah; it does not prove that if the ban came from an earlier revealed law.
rows.anchor: وفيه دليل على جواز نسخ السنة بالكتاب إن كانت حرمة الأكل والشرب والجماع ثابتة بالسنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What God has prescribed includes the offspring He decreed; intercourse should aim at children and continuity, the purpose of desire and marriage, not pleasure alone.
rows.anchor: واطلبوا ما قدره الله تعالى وأثبته في اللوح المحفوظ من الولد وفيه أن المباشر ينبغي أن يكون غرضه الولد

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A prophetic saying urges marriage and reproduction so the Muslim community may be numerous before other nations on Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: "تناكحوا تناسلوا تكثروا فإني أباهي بكم الأمم يوم القيامة"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The white thread is the first thin line of dawn; the black thread is the dark remainder of night beside it as true dawn spreads across the horizon.
rows.anchor: هو أول ما يبدو من بياض النهار كالخيط الممدود دقيقا ثم ينتشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase 'of dawn' explains the white thread, while the black thread is understood as being of night.
rows.anchor: {من الفجر} أي : انشقاق عمود الصبح بيان للخيط الأبيض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dawn clause limits intercourse, eating, and drinking alike; allowing sex until dawn entails that one may delay ritual washing and still begin the fast while in a state of major impurity.
rows.anchor: غاية للأمور الثلاثة أي : المباشرة والأكل والشرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fasting means continued abstention from intercourse, food, and drink throughout the daylight, ending when night begins at sunset.
rows.anchor: {ثم أتموا الصيام} أي : أديموا الإمساك عن المباشرة والأكل والشرب

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The fast-breaking time arrives when night comes, day departs, and the sun has set; the three signs clarify that the full disk must disappear or help observers who cannot see sunset.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث "إذا أقبل الليل وأدبر النهار وغابت الشمس فقد أفطر الصائم"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some infer daytime intention for Ramadan from the command to complete the fast: since fasting begins after dawn and entails intention, the command includes forming intention then.
rows.anchor: لأن الله تعالى لما أباح المباشرة والأكل والشرب إلى الفجر تبين أن ابتداء الصوم يكون بعد الفجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some infer that continuous fasting is excluded because night is the fast's endpoint and breaking the fast follows.
rows.anchor: وأما الثاني فلأن الله تعالى جعل الليل غاية الصوم وغاية الشيء مقطعه فيكون بعدها الإفطار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Others say the verse only marks the end of the duty; since the permission commands are concessions rather than obligations, it does not establish that fasting at night is forbidden or disprove continuous fasting.
rows.anchor: قال بعضهم : الليل غاية وجوب الصوم فإذا دخل الليل لا يجب الصوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because people might compare retreat to fasting and assume sex is forbidden only by day, the passage clarifies that intercourse is prohibited for a person in retreat as well.
rows.anchor: ولما ظن أن حال الاعتكاف كحال الصوم في أن المباشرة تحرم فيه نهارا لا ليلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iʿtikāf is remaining in a mosque with the intention of worship and drawing near to God; it is an ancient religious practice, also mentioned in the command to purify the House for worshippers and retreatants.
rows.anchor: وهو في الشرع لزوم المسجد والمكث لطاعة الله فيه والتقرب إليه وهو من الشرائع القديمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse was revealed about retreatants who left the mosque to have sex and returned after washing; intercourse is forbidden and invalidates iʿtikāf.
rows.anchor: نزلت فيمن كان يعتكف في المسجد فإذا عرضت له حاجة إلى امرأته خرج فجامعها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural 'mosques' implies retreat is valid in any mosque, though a congregational mosque is better to avoid leaving for Friday prayer.
rows.anchor: ولفظ المساجد يدل على جواز الاعتكاف في كل مسجد إلا أن المسجد الجامع أفضل حتى لا يحتاج إلى الخروج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sincere iʿtikāf is among the most honored acts because it empties the heart of everything besides God.
rows.anchor: والاعتكاف من أشرف الأعمال إذا كان عن إخلاص لأن فيه تفريغ القلب عما سوى الله تعالى

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: ʿAṭāʾ compares a retreatant to someone who sits at a powerful patron's door, refusing to leave until the need is fulfilled; the retreatant waits in God's house for forgiveness.
rows.anchor: قال عطاء مثل المعتكف كرجل له حاجة إلى عظيم فيجلس على بابه ويقول : لا أبرح

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A hadith likens helping a brother in need to twenty years of iʿtikāf and says one day of retreat places three trenches between a person and Hell, each farther apart than the horizons.
rows.anchor: من مشى في حاجة أخيه فكأنما اعتكف عشرين سنة ومن اعتكف يوما جعل الله بينه وبين النار ثلاثة خندق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Retreat and seclusion spare people from one another's harm, humble the self, turn it from worldly concerns, and begin the path to sincerity.
rows.anchor: يسلم منه الناس وسلم هو منهم وفيها خمول النفس والإعراض عن الدنيا وهو أول طريق الصدق والإخلاص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seclusion cultivates intimacy with God, reliance, and contentment with sufficiency; social dealings can lead people to blur lawful and unlawful limits.
rows.anchor: وفيه الإنس بالله والتوكل والرضى بالكفاف فإن المعاشر للناس والمخالط يتكلف في معيشته البتة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The solitary also avoids ingratiating himself with people and many other sins that commonly arise through social mixing.
rows.anchor: ويسلم المتخلي أيضا من مداهنة الناس وغير ذلك من المعاصي التي يتعرض الإنسان لها غالبا بالمخالطة

rows.speaker: افتاده أفندي
rows.claim: Tasawwuf means avoiding anything tainted by unlawfulness and guarding the tongue from idle speech; this discipline can be practiced among people, more firmly than through retreat alone.
rows.anchor: التصوف عبارة عن الاجتناب عن كل ما فيه شائبة الحرمة وصون لسانه عن الكلام اللغو

rows.speaker: افتاده أفندي
rows.claim: The Prophetic and Companion path is not a prescribed forty-day retreat: the Prophet practiced retreat in Ramadan's last ten days, while Moses alone was appointed forty nights.
rows.anchor: فطريقنا طريق النبي عليه السلام وطريق الأصحاب رضي الله تعالى عنهم والنبي عليه السلام لم يعين الأربعين

rows.speaker: افتاده أفندي
rows.claim: The Khalwati order derives its forty-day retreat from Moses' appointment, not from a Prophetic prescription.
rows.anchor: نعم فعل ذلك موسى عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's limits separate truth from falsehood and block violations; believers are told not even to approach them, which more strongly prevents transgression.
rows.anchor: وجعل ما شرعه الله تعالى لعباده من الأحكام حدودا لهم لكونها أمورا حاجزة بين الحق والباطل

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet compares God's prohibitions to a king's protected pasture: grazing around it risks entering it.
rows.anchor: إن لكل ملك حمى وإن حمى الله محارمه فمن رتع حول الحمى يوشك أن يقع فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's clear explanation of signs is guidance and mercy meant to lead people to obey His commands and avoid His prohibitions.
rows.anchor: والمقصود من تعظيم البيان هدايته ورحمته على عباده في هذا البيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taqwa proceeds by avoiding shirk first, then sins, then disordered desires.
rows.anchor: والتقوى اتقاء الشرك. ثم بعده اتقاء المعاصي والسيئات. ثم بعده اتقاء الشهوات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Delight in worldly possessions signals distance from God; relying on what one holds shows weak trust, and turning to people in hardship shows that one has not truly known God.
rows.anchor: فرحك بشيء من الدنيا دليل على بعدك من الله

rows.speaker: السعدي
rows.claim: Saʿdī's poem reflects on worldly pride and death: rulers die and are buried, and only a good or bad name remains from what each person cultivated.
rows.anchor: برفتند وهركس درود آنه كشت نماند يجز نام نيكو وزشت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The supplication asks for long lives joined to good deeds, short hopes, and complete understanding.
rows.anchor: اللهم اجعلنا من الذين طال عمرهم وحسن عملهم وقصر أملهم وكمل عقلهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase 'or like the one' coordinates with the preceding 'did you not see'; it means 'or did you see someone like this,' using comparison because many reject resurrection and even more doubt how it occurs.
rows.anchor: عطف على قوله ألم تر وتقديره أو رأيت مثل الذي فعل كذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passerby is ʿUzayr ibn Sharḥiyā, and the ruined town is Jerusalem, the most widely accepted and strongest identification; qarya derives from gathering people.
rows.anchor: والمار هو عزير بن شرخيا والقرية بيت المقدس على الأشهر الأظهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The historical account says Nebuchadnezzar came with six hundred thousand standards, ruined Jerusalem, killed some Israelites, left some in Syria, and deported others as captives distributed among his kings.
rows.anchor: فسار إليهم في ستمائة ألف راية حتى وطىء الشام وخرب بيت المقدس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The city lay empty with its roofs collapsed over the walls; the root of خاوية describes an emptied interior or a house that fell in.
rows.anchor: خالية عن أهلها وساقطة على سقوفها بأن سقطت العروش ثم الحيطان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿUzayr asks how God will rebuild the ruined city itself; he is expressing ordinary human astonishment, not doubt in God's power.
rows.anchor: الله تعالى هذه القرية بعد خرابها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the narrated setting, ʿUzayr rests under a tree, leaves his donkey, explores the empty town, eats its figs and grapes, drinks pressed grapes, and falls asleep.
rows.anchor: نزل تحت ظل شجرة وهو على حمار فربط حماره وطاف في القرية ولم ير بها أحدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God causes the young ʿUzayr and his donkey to die in sleep, while concealing their bodies from people and animals.
rows.anchor: فأماته الله في منامه وهو شاب وكان معه شيء من التين والعنب والعصير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After seventy years, a Persian ruler called Yūshak arrives with a thousand stewards and vast labor crews to rebuild Jerusalem.
rows.anchor: فلما مضى من موته سبعون سنة وجه الله ملكا عظيما من ملوك فارس يقال له يوشك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account says Nebuchadnezzar dies from a mosquito in his brain, the surviving Israelites return, and the city flourishes again over thirty years.
rows.anchor: وأهلك الله بخت نصر ببعوضة دخلت دماغه ونجى الله من بقي من بني إسرائيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After a century, God raises ʿUzayr; the verb بعث suggests his return as before, intelligent and able to reason about divine realities, more fully than the verb أحياه would.
rows.anchor: وإنما قال ثم بعثه ولم يقل ثم أحياه لأن قوله ثم بعثه يدل على أنه عاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question about how long he had remained may come from God or a commissioned angel, and is meant to expose the limit of his knowledge and extinguish any sense that the interval was short.
rows.anchor: أو ملك مأمور من قبله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The century-long preservation of food is another extraordinary sign, since food naturally deteriorates.
rows.anchor: وهو إبقاء الغذاء المتسارع إلى الفساد بالطبع على ما كان عليه دهرا طويلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says the figs and grapes remained as freshly picked and the grape juice as freshly pressed.
rows.anchor: روي أنه وجد تينه وعنبه كما جني وعصيره كما عصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause about not changing is a circumstantial phrase that can appear with or without a conjunction; food and drink take a singular pronoun because they act as one nourishment.
rows.anchor: والجملة المنفية حال بغير واو من الطعام والشراب لأن المضارع المنفي إذا وقع حالا يجوز أن يكون بالواو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hāʾ in لم يتسنه may be a root letter, from سنهة, or a pause hāʾ from سنوة; 'not change' expresses the implication that years have not passed.
rows.anchor: والهاء في لم يتسنه إن كانت أصلية فهو من السنة التي أصلها سنهة وإن كانت هاء سكت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The donkey's scattered, broken bones make the long elapsed time visible and reassure ʿUzayr.
rows.anchor: كيف نخرت عظامه وتفرقت وتقطعت أوصاله وتمزقت ليتبين لك ما ذكر من لبثك المديد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God preserves the food and revives ʿUzayr and his donkey as a sign for the people of that century, including a chance to learn Torah knowledge lost across generations.
rows.anchor: فعلنا ذلك أي : إحياءك وإحياء حمارك وحفظ ما معك من الطعام والشراب لنجعلك آية للناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated command to inspect the bones shifts attention from elapsed time to the process of reviving another body, after ʿUzayr has witnessed his own revival.
rows.anchor: تكرير الأمر مع أن المراد عظام الحمار أيضا لما أن المأمور به أولا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb ننشزها means lifting and reassembling the bones into their proper places; the clause may describe their living state or stand for their condition.
rows.anchor: نرفع بعضها من الأرض إلى بعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Flesh is singular because the bones are visibly separate while flesh appears connected; the account leaves the breathing of spirit unexplained because it is not needed here.
rows.anchor: لأن العظام متفرقة متعددة صورة واللحم متصل متحد مشاهدة ولعل عدم التعرض لكيفية نفخ الروح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A heavenly voice commands the scattered bones to rejoin; bones, nerves, veins, flesh, skin, and hair return in order, then the spirit is breathed in and the donkey stands braying.
rows.anchor: أيتها العظام البالية المتفرقة إن الله يأمرك أن ينضم بعضك إلى بعض كما كان وتكتسى لحما وجلدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After he sees the dead revived, ʿUzayr recognizes that God's power encompasses every possible thing, including the wonders he witnessed.
rows.anchor: ظهر له إحياء الميت عيانا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Back home, ʿUzayr finds an old blind, disabled woman who knew him; he prays and restores her sight and mobility, and she recognizes him.
rows.anchor: فإذا هو بعجوز عمياء مقعدة قد أدركت زمن عزير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His descendants initially doubt the returned ʿUzayr, but his adult son verifies him by a distinctive crescent-shaped black mark between his shoulders.
rows.anchor: وكان في المجلس ابن العزير قد بلغ مائة وثماني عشرة سنة وبنو بنيه شيوخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report says Nebuchadnezzar killed forty thousand Torah reciters, leaving no copy or living expert; ʿUzayr recites it from memory, and a buried manuscript is found and matches him letter for letter.
rows.anchor: وقد كان قتل بخت نصر بيت المقدس من قراء التوراة أربعين ألف رجل ولم يكن يومئذ بينهم نسخة من التوراة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The parable compares the expenditure, not the people themselves, to a seed, since a human being is not like an inanimate plant.
rows.anchor: لأن الذين ينفقون لا يشبهون الحبة لأنه لا يشبه الحيوان بالجماد بل نفقاتهم تشبه الحبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Spending in God's path covers both obligatory and voluntary forms of charitable good; a seed planted in fertile land yields seven stalks, each with a hundred grains.
rows.anchor: في وجوه الخيرات من الواجب كالزكاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The seven-hundredfold crop is observable in productive land and may be exceeded by some grains.
rows.anchor: كما يشاهد ذلك في الذرة والدخن في الأراضي المغلة بل أكثر من ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God may multiply the reward further according to His will and the giver's sincerity and effort, which explains why rewards differ.
rows.anchor: تلك المضاعفة إلى ما شاء الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's abundance is unrestricted, and He knows the giver's intention, amount, and how the money was earned.
rows.anchor: {والله واسع} لا يضيق عليه ما يتفضل به من الزيادة {عليم} بنية المنفق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Like a skilled farmer with good seed and fertile soil, a righteous giver with wholesome wealth who places it properly receives greater growth.
rows.anchor: إذا كان صالحا والمال طيبا ووضع في موضعه يكون الثواب أكثر

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra transmits the Prophet's teaching that God accepts only wholesome earnings and grows even a single date of charity until it is mountain-sized.
rows.anchor: عن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه عن النبي عليه السلام أنه قال : "من تصدق بعدل تمرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet's image of God nurturing a charitable gift signals that charity needs this special cultivation because love of wealth tends to diminish its quality.
rows.anchor: وإنما ذكر النبي عليه السلام التربية في الصدقة وإن كان غيرها من العبادات يزيد أيضا بقبوله

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A hadith says a believer's charity protects its giver from worldly calamities, the trial of the grave, and the punishment of Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: "صدقة المؤمن تدفع عن صاحبها آفات الدنيا وفتنة القبر وعذاب يوم القيامة"

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A prophetic parable depicts generosity as a tree rooted in Paradise and miserliness as one rooted in Hell, each drawing followers toward its destination.
rows.anchor: "السخاوة شجرة أصلها في الجنة وأغصانها متدليات في دار الدنيا

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Earning support for a widow and a poor person is likened to jihad because caring for them demands patience and struggle against the self.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث "الساعي على الأرملة والمسكين كالمجاهد في سبيل الله"

rows.speaker: السعدي
rows.claim: Saʿdī's poem recounts ʿUmar ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz selling his precious gem-set ring during a famine and giving the proceeds to the needy rather than remain comfortable while citizens suffered.
rows.anchor: قضارا در آمد يكى خشك سال كه شد بدر سيماى مردم هلال

rows.speaker: السعدي
rows.claim: The poem praises preferring people's comfort over one's own and refusing to keep luxury while the poor are distressed.
rows.anchor: مرا شايد انكشترى بى نكين نشايد دل خلق اندوهكين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Deeds depend on intentions; the report that a believer's intention is better than his deed means better than a nonbeliever's deed when the believer intended a good act but another dug the well first.
rows.anchor: مورد الحديث أن عثمان رضي الله تعالى عنه سمع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه وعد بثواب عظيم على حفر بئر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative explanation is that a believer's intention alone is better than action performed without intention; some acts need intention, such as prayer, while recitation and remembrance may not.
rows.anchor: والجواب الثاني أن النية المجردة من المؤمن خير من عمله المجرد عن النية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ordinary believers spend wealth for Paradise, while the elect spend by purifying their character and heart, hoping for the vision of God on Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: وإنفاق الخواص إصلاح الحال بتزكية النفس وتصفية القلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The spenders put wealth in its proper place; ثم signals the high rank of adding restraint from boasting and harm after the gift.
rows.anchor: {ثم} لإظهار علو رتبة المعطوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mann is reminding recipients of one's favor as if they now owe a debt; harm includes reproaching them for ingratitude, repeated requests, or annoyance.
rows.anchor: وهو أن يعتد على من أحسن إليه بإحسانه ويريه أنه أوجب بذلك عليه حقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who give without boasting or harm receive their reward from God, face no fear of future punishment, and do not grieve over worldly things left behind.
rows.anchor: ثوابهم في الآخرة وتخلية الخبر عن الفاء المفيدة لسببية ما قبلها لما بعدها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A story says Hasan ibn ʿAli sells Fatima's shirt for six dirhams, gives the money to a beggar, then arranges a deferred camel purchase and resale; the Prophet identifies the beggar, seller, and buyer as angels.
rows.anchor: روي أن الحسن بن علي رضي الله عنهما اشتهى طعاما فباع قميص فاطمة بستة دراهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some exegetes say the two verses concern ʿUthmān, who equipped the Tabuk army with a thousand camels and a thousand dinars, and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn ʿAwf, who gave half his wealth.
rows.anchor: قال بعض أهل التفسير نزلت هذه الآية والتي قبلها في عثمان وعبد الرحمن رضي الله عنهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet prayed that God be pleased with ʿUthmān; he blessed ʿAbd al-Raḥmān's retained and donated money, and both gave without boasting or hurting recipients.
rows.anchor: يقول : "يا رب رضيت عنه فارض عنه"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One opinion compares boasting to hypocrisy and harm to ostentation.
rows.anchor: قال بعضهم المن يشبه بالنفاق والأذى يشبه بالرياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Scholars differ on consequences: one view denies reward and assigns sin, Wahb denies both reward and sin, and another preserves the basic reward but removes multiplication and adds sin for boasting.
rows.anchor: قال وهب فلا أجر له ولا وزر له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although God may bestow favor on His servants, humans cannot boast: God's ownership and power are complete, while any virtue in a servant comes from God.
rows.anchor: وذلك لأن الله تعالى تام الملك والقدرة وملكه وقدرته ليس بغيره والعبد وإن كان فيه خصال الخير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The recipient already feels humbled by need; displaying the gift further crushes the recipient and turns a benefit into harm and mistreatment.
rows.anchor: فإذا أضاف المعطي إلى ذلك إظهار ذلك الإنعام زاد ذلك في انكسار قلبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A gracious response means turning away a petitioner kindly; forgiveness covers overlooking persistent or burdensome requests.
rows.anchor: رد جميل وهو أن يرد السائل بطريق جميل حسن تقبله القلوب والطباع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A kind refusal and pardon are better than a gift followed by harm, because one who both helps and injures the poor loses the reward.
rows.anchor: خير من صدقة يتبعها أذى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent puzzle—how a harmful charity can still be called good—is answered by reading the comparison from the hearers' limited perspective, as in the cited verse about trade and amusement.
rows.anchor: فإن قالوا : أي : خير في الصدقة التي فيها أذى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God needs no charity and can provide the poor by another route; His forbearance delays punishment for boastful givers but does not excuse them.
rows.anchor: عما عندكم من الصدقة لا يحوج الفقراء إلى تحمل مؤونة المن والأذى

rows.speaker: الهدائي
rows.claim: A gracious refusal lifts the petitioner's heart and spirit, while charity first benefits the body; spiritual relief outweighs bodily benefit spoiled by hurtful words.
rows.anchor: وإنما كان الرد الجميل خيرا من صدقة المان والمؤذي لأن القول الحسن وإن كان بالرد

rows.speaker: الشعبي
rows.claim: Al-Shaʿbī says a donor who does not consider himself more needy for charity's reward than the poor person is for the gift has invalidated his charity.
rows.anchor: قال الشعبي من لم ير نفسه إلى ثواب الصدقة أحوج من الفقير إلى صدقته فقد أبطل صدقته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Early Muslims guarded against ostentation because it is common and ruinous; in the grave ostentation becomes a snake and miserliness a scorpion, and indulging one vice feeds it.
rows.anchor: وبالغ السلف في الصدقة والتحرز فيها عن الرياء فإنه غالب على النفس وهو مهلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Invalidating charity means losing its reward, not undoing the completed act; boasting and harm earn no reward and incur wrong against the recipient.
rows.anchor: والمراد بإبطال الصدقة إحباط أجرها لأن الصدقة لما وقعت وتقدمت لم يمكن أن يراد بإبطالها نفسها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The comparison is to a hypocrite who spends to be seen and praised, without belief or hope for God's approval and the afterlife.
rows.anchor: المراد المنافق لأن الكافر معلن كفره غير مراء والكاف في محل النصب على أنه صفة لمصدر محذوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Riyāʾ is a reciprocal form because the giver acts while attending to the people's seeing and praise.
rows.anchor: ومعنى المفاعلة ههنا مبني على أن المرائي في الإنفاق يراعي أن تراه الناس فيحمدوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṣafwān is a smooth stone with a little dust; a heavy downpour strips it bare so no covering remains.
rows.anchor: حجر صاف أملس وهو واحد وجمع فمن جعله جمعا فواحده صفوانة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dissemblers cannot benefit from what they earned or receive any reward, like deeds made scattered dust in the cited verse.
rows.anchor: لا ينتفعون بما فعلوا رئاء ولا يجدون له ثوابا قطعا كقوله تعالى : {فجعلناه هباء منثورا}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural pronoun refers to the generic individual or group represented by الذي; the singular relative can also convey the sense of من.
rows.anchor: أراد بالذي ينفق الجنس أو الفريق الذي ينفق ولأن من والذي يتعاقبان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The parable first makes the clearest case—a disbeliever's worthless spending—then compares its stripping away to the loss of charity's reward through boasting and harm.
rows.anchor: فمثله أولا بمن ينفق ماله رئاء الناس وهو مع ذلك كافر بالله واليوم الآخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Muʿtazilite account treats good works as establishing reward that major sins can erase; the author's Ashʿarite colleagues say no reward had been established because the gift was never sincerely devotional.
rows.anchor: وذلك صريح في القول بالإحباط والتكفير كما ذهب إليه المعتزلة القائلون بأن الأعمال الصالحة توجب الثواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author favors the Ashʿarite reading: reward is a pure divine gift, and boasting makes the gift a donation to the recipient rather than a sincere deed offered to God for promised reward.
rows.anchor: فقد جرى على سنن المبادلة التي وقعت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since good deeds are treated as a loan or transaction with God, a donor should not boast to the poor; boasting turns away from God and means the deed was empty from the start.
rows.anchor: فلما كانت معاملته في الحقيقة مع الله تعالى لم يبق وجه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning about God not guiding disbelievers implies that ostentation, boasting, and injury are traits believers must avoid.
rows.anchor: وفيه تعريض بأن كلا من الرئاء والمن والأذى من خصائص الكفار ولا بد للمؤمنين أن يجتنبوها

rows.speaker: بعض العلماء
rows.claim: An unnamed scholar compares ostentatious worship to carrying a sack of stones: observers may praise its fullness, but it buys nothing.
rows.anchor: روي عن بعض العلماء أنه قال مثل من يعمل الطاعة للرئاء والسمعة كمثل رجل خرج إلى السوق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Early donors hid charity in several ways: seeking blind recipients, attaching money to a sleeping poor person's clothing, or leaving it where a poor person would find it.
rows.anchor: وقد بالغ السلف في إخفاء صدقتهم عن أعين الناس حتى طلب بعضهم فقيرا أعمى

rows.speaker: جلال الدين الرومي
rows.claim: Rumi's poem urges worshippers to seek God's guidance and ask that prayer not be mixed with the prayer of the misguided or ostentatious.
rows.anchor: كفت يغمبر بيك صاحب ريا

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet calls ostentation the minor shirk he fears for the community and says God will tell those who sought human notice to seek their reward from those people.
rows.anchor: قال النبي صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم : "إن أخوف ما أخاف عليكم الشرك الأصغر"

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A hadith says a Qur'an reciter, a martyr, and a wealthy donor are first brought to judgment; each is condemned for seeking fame rather than God's approval and becomes fuel for Hell.
rows.anchor: أول من يدعى به رجل جمع القرآن ورجل قتل في سبيل الله ورجل كثير المال

rows.speaker: السعدي
rows.claim: Saʿdī's Persian verses urge humility, hiding spiritual emptiness, and resisting the wish for public fame or praise.
rows.anchor: طريقت همينست كاهل يقين نكو كار بودند وتقصير بين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the inward reading, transactions mixed with ulterior aims turn away from God and toward falsehood, thereby invalidating acts of devotion; after truth there is only error.
rows.anchor: والإشارة في الآية في المعاملات إذا كانت مشوبة بالأغراض ففيها نوع من الأعراض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reminding a poor person of charity shows the giver sought the recipient rather than God; if the goal were God, the giver would feel indebted to the poor person as a means of reaching Him.
rows.anchor: إذا مننت بها على الفقير فقد أعرضت عن طلب الحق لأن قصدك في الصدقة لو كان طلب الحق

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The hadith that the rich would perish without the poor is interpreted to mean that poor recipients give the rich a way to reach God.
rows.anchor: قال صلى الله عليه وسلم "لولا الفقراء لهلك الأغنياء" معناه لم يجدوا وسيلة إلى الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation reverses 'the upper hand is better': the poor person has the upper hand and the rich donor the lower, since the donor gives and receives through the poor.
rows.anchor: وقد فسر بعضهم قوله عليه السلام : "اليد العليا خير من اليد السفلى" بأن اليد العليا هي يد الفقير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the inward reading, harm means turning toward anything other than the Real, which corrupts acts when they are mixed with worldly or otherworldly motives.
rows.anchor: والأذى هو الإقبال على الباطل لأن كل شيء غير الحق فهو باطل

rows.speaker: جلال الدين الرومي
rows.claim: Rumi's poetry says the lover's joy and grief, service, and wage belong to the beloved; love for any other gain is a futile fantasy.
rows.anchor: عاشقا نرا شادماني وغم اوست دست مزد واجرت خدمت هم اوست

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When divine love dominates the heart, it severs attachment to wealth, children, and one's own life as rival claims.
rows.anchor: فالعشق الإلهي والحب الرحماني إذا استولى على قلب العبد يقطع عنه عرق الشركة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A spiritually mature servant does not serve for wages; trusting the master's generosity frees the heart from watching for payment.
rows.anchor: والخدمة بالأجرة لا تناسب الرجولية فإن من علم أن مولاه كريم يقطع قلبه عن ملاحظة الأجرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeking God's pleasure with expenditure stabilizes part of the self against innate love of wealth and reluctance to spend; the soul can be trained despite its natural inclinations.
rows.anchor: جعل بعض أنفسهم ثابتا على الإيمان والطاعة ليزول عنها رذيلة البخل وحب المال

rows.speaker: البوصيري
rows.claim: The Burda compares the self to a child: if left alone it grows attached to nursing, but if weaned it can be weaned.
rows.anchor: والنفس كالطفل إن تهمله شب على

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Neglect strengthens idleness and miserliness; imposing difficult bodily and financial worship brings the self into line and purifies it of acquired habits.
rows.anchor: فمتى أهملتها فقد تمرنت واعتادت الكسل والبطالة والبخل وإمساك المال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preposition من can mean 'some of,' as in the idiom about shaking some liveliness from one's sleeve.
rows.anchor: فمن تبعيضية كما في قولهم : "هز من عطفه وحرك من نشاطه"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wealth counts as part of the self because of the soul's intense attachment to it; giving money stabilizes a part of oneself, while giving life and money gives the whole self.
rows.anchor: إن النفس لشدة تعلقها بالمال كأنه بعض منها فالمال شقيق الروح

rows.speaker: جلال الدين الرومي
rows.claim: Rumi's verses distinguish giving money from giving one's life for God and say God repays each with the corresponding gift.
rows.anchor: آن درم دادن سخى را لايق است

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second reading takes تثبيتا as making something true and firm: spending confirms faith rooted in the heart and confidence that God rewards good action.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون التثبيت بمعنى جعل الشيء صادقا محققا ثابتا والمعنى تصديقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On this reading من marks the origin of faith in the heart, as in the cited phrase 'envy from themselves.'
rows.anchor: فمن لابتداء الغاية كما في قوله تعالى : {حسدا من عند أنفسهم}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A garden on a raised hill enjoys gentle air and protection from hail, yielding better-looking trees and sweeter fruit than low ground with stagnant air.
rows.anchor: مكان مرتفع مأمون من أن يصطلمه البرد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The continuation cites a Hafiz couplet advising the servant to trust the master's generosity instead of demanding wages.
rows.anchor: تو بندكى وكدايان بشرط مزد مكن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The closing prayer asks God to sever hope from everything else and make the worshippers seek only His essence.
rows.anchor: اللهم اقطع رجاءنا عن غيرك واجعلنا من الذين لا يطلبون منك إلا ذاتك
